name: WEYERHAEUSER COMPANY
share_adj_basis: applied to revenue components only (v5.4); OE/share CAGR enters unadjusted

overrides_applied.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-13, accession 0001193125-26-051422), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, investing activities: 'Capital expenditures for property and equipment' $423M for FY2025, $364M for FY2024, $390M for FY2023, plus 'Capital expenditures for timberlands reforestation' $51M / $52M / $57M for the same years — combined totals $474M / $416M / $447M; corroborated in EDGAR companyfacts under us-gaap PropertyPlantAndEquipmentAdditions with identical totals ($474M / $416M / $447M) and by the same filing's FAD reconciliation line 'Capital expenditures' ($474M for FY2025, $416M for FY2024)
overrides_applied.reason: DATA_GAP:capex — capex missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 (in fact every year from FY2019) under every candidate tag the engine reads: the us-gaap PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment tag carries no filed value after FY2018 ($368M), and Weyerhaeuser files its two cash capex lines only in the combined total tagged PropertyPlantAndEquipmentAdditions, which the engine does not read. The engine applies this single value to every missing period; the value used is $447M, the median of the three filed years and the exact FY2023 figure. Against the true per-year totals it overstates FY2024 capex by $31M (true $416M, conservative direction — lowers that year's OE) and understates FY2025 capex by $27M (true $474M, raising the trough FY2025 OE from $45M to $72M; FY2025 is not the median year). The resulting median base ($0.71/share) sits below the median built from the true per-year figures ($0.75/share), so the approximation is conservative on the base that sets the tier. 'Acquisition of timberlands' ($469M / $251M / $233M for FY2025/24/23, same statement) is excluded: the filer presents it separately as land M&A, not capital expenditures.

fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Real Estate sector — OE/capex DCF fits real estate names poorly; grade confidence low

OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex — filing gap in the last 3 FY filled by a judgment override (filing: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-13, accession 0001193125-26-051422), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, investing activities: 'Capital expenditures for property and equipment' $423M for FY2025, $364M for FY2024, $390M for FY2023, plus 'Capital expenditures for timberlands reforestation' $51M / $52M / $57M for the same years — combined totals $474M / $416M / $447M; corroborated in EDGAR companyfacts under us-gaap PropertyPlantAndEquipmentAdditions with identical totals ($474M / $416M / $447M) and by the same filing's FAD reconciliation line 'Capital expenditures' ($474M for FY2025, $416M for FY2024)); an override never replaces a filed value — see overrides_applied and override_impact
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 0.10 vs 3-yr median 0.71 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 11.7x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 9.9x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases

override_impact.basis: engine-native normalized base (median of last 3 FY) and weighted IRR, DCF run both ways (zero-fill baseline vs with-override); a --base-oe-ps TTM base is excluded from both sides — its override effect shows in ttm.py output
